g1.label: 1. You ___ have a valid passport
g1.why: A passport is required to travel abroad, so use 'must' for an obligation.

g2.label: 2. Volunteers ___ follow the safety rules
g2.why: 'At all times' shows a rule everyone must follow, so use 'have to'.

g3.label: 3. You ___ touch wild animals
g3.why: 'Mustn't' means it is not allowed, because it can be dangerous.

g4.label: 4. You ___ speak the local language
g4.why: 'Don't have to' means it isn't necessary, because English is often enough.

g5.label: 5. Younger volunteers ___ get permission
g5.why: Written permission is required, so use 'have to' for the obligation.

g6.label: 6. You ___ leave the group without telling
g6.why: 'Mustn't' shows something forbidden: leaving without telling a supervisor.

g7.label: 7. Volunteers ___ bring their own tools
g7.why: The project provides tools, so it isn't necessary: 'don't have to'.

g8.label: 8. Everyone ___ attend the safety briefing
g8.why: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb, so the obligation is 'has to'.

g1.label: 1. You ___ research the organisation
g1.why: 'Should' gives advice; researching first is a good idea.

g2.label: 2. You ___ travel without telling your family
g2.why: This is advice, not a rule, so use 'shouldn't' for something that's a bad idea.

g3.label: 3. New volunteers ___ ask questions
g3.why: 'Should' gives advice: asking questions is a good idea when you're unsure.

g4.label: 4. You ___ learn a few basic phrases
g4.why: Learning a few phrases is good advice, so use 'should'.

g5.label: 5. You ___ ignore the advice of local staff
g5.why: Ignoring local staff is a bad idea, so the advice is 'shouldn't'.

g6.label: 6. It ___ be a good idea to pack light
g6.why: 'Should' recommends something: packing light is sensible advice.

g7.label: 7. You ___ keep an open mind
g7.why: Keeping an open mind about other cultures is good advice: 'should'.

g8.label: 8. You ___ compare everything to home
g8.why: Comparing everything to home is a bad idea, so the advice is 'shouldn't'.
